claims.text: The Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy is produced by additive manufacturing.
The additively manufactured alloy contains dual nanoprecipitation.
In-situ TEM equipped with an environmental cell can elucidate mechanistic aspects of oxidation in this alloy.
In-situ environmental-cell TEM can reveal elemental redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
The proposed observations are to be performed under high-temperature conditions.
Nanoprecipitates are the structural feature through which oxidation behavior and elemental redistribution will be investigated.
Applying in-situ environmental-cell TEM will improve understanding of high-temperature oxidation behavior and nanoprecipitate-related elemental redistribution.
Current understanding of oxidation behavior and nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution at high temperatures is limited.
The exact ability of in-situ environmental-cell TEM to provide real-time analysis of microstructural changes and elemental migration remains uncertain without experimentation.
